title: Grade 4 Science — Fri, May 22
description: Food & Nutrition — Day 5 of 5: Synthesis — nutrients, digestion, and food safety
subject: science

questions.question: A child eats only bread daily. Which nutrient is likely deficient?
questions.explanation: Bread provides carbohydrates but lacks sufficient proteins (for growth), vitamins (immunity), and minerals (bones, blood).

questions.question: Match: Vitamin A → ___, Vitamin C → ___, Vitamin D → ___
options: Night blindness prevention / Scurvy prevention / Rickets prevention
Scurvy prevention / Rickets prevention / Night blindness prevention
questions.explanation: Vitamin A → prevents night blindness. Vitamin C → prevents scurvy. Vitamin D → prevents rickets.

questions.question: Riya has pale skin, low energy, and breathes quickly. Which mineral deficiency could cause this?
questions.explanation: Iron deficiency causes anaemia — low haemoglobin means less oxygen transported, leading to fatigue, paleness, and breathlessness.

questions.question: Put the digestion sequence in order: (A) Absorption in small intestine (B) Mouth chewing (C) Stomach acid breakdown (D) Waste excretion
questions.explanation: Digestion order: Mouth (B) → Stomach (C) → Small intestine absorption (A) → Excretion (D).

questions.question: An Indian breakfast of poha (rice flakes) + milk + banana provides:
questions.explanation: This balanced breakfast: poha (carbs), milk (protein, calcium, Vitamin D), banana (Vitamin B6, potassium, fibre).

questions.question: Left-over dal from the morning is still in the pot at 8pm in summer. Is it safe to eat?
options: Maybe — it should be boiled again before eating
questions.explanation: In hot weather, cooked food left unrefrigerated for hours can develop harmful bacteria. Always reheat to boiling before eating.

questions.question: Why do athletes need more carbohydrates and proteins than less active people?
options: Carbs provide energy for activity; proteins repair micro-tears in muscles from exercise
No reason — diet should be the same
questions.explanation: Carbohydrates fuel activity. Exercise causes micro-tears in muscles that need protein to repair and grow stronger.

questions.question: A bottle of juice says 'no preservatives added.' How should it be stored?
options: In the refrigerator and consumed within a few days
In sunlight to keep it fresh
questions.explanation: No preservatives = microorganisms will grow faster. Refrigerate and consume quickly (2–3 days after opening).

questions.question: Which is the MOST complete meal for a growing child?
questions.explanation: Khichdi provides carbs+protein. Vegetables+salad give vitamins and fibre. Curd adds calcium. Fruit adds Vitamin C. Truly balanced.

questions.question: Vitamin B12 deficiency (common in vegans) causes problems with:
options: Nerve function and red blood cell production
questions.explanation: Vitamin B12 (found mainly in animal products) is needed for nerve health and red blood cell formation. Vegans must supplement.

questions.question: Which organ produces both digestive juices AND hormones?
questions.explanation: The pancreas is both exocrine (digestive enzymes) and endocrine (insulin and glucagon hormones for blood sugar control).

questions.question: Why should raw meat be kept separate from vegetables in the fridge?
options: To prevent cross-contamination — bacteria from meat can infect vegetables
No reason — it does not matter
questions.explanation: Raw meat may carry harmful bacteria (Salmonella, E. coli) that can transfer to vegetables through contact or dripping.

questions.question: A food label says: Calories 250, Protein 10g, Fat 12g, Carbs 28g. Which nutrient provides most energy here?
questions.explanation: Fat provides 9 kcal/g vs 4 kcal/g for protein and carbs. 12g fat = 108 kcal. 28g carbs = 112 kcal. Carbs give most total calories here, but fat is more calorie-dense per gram.

questions.question: The 'best before' date on food packaging means:
options: The food is dangerous after this date
The food is at best quality before this date; may be safe but less optimal after
This is when the food was made
This is the expiry date only for medicines
questions.explanation: 'Best before' = optimal quality guaranteed before this date. 'Use by' is the safety date. Best before ≠ 'expires and is dangerous.'

questions.question: Week synthesis: the most accurate statement about food and nutrition is:
options: We only need carbohydrates for good health
A balanced diet includes all nutrients; food preservation keeps food safe; digestion converts food into absorbable nutrients
Proteins are not needed if you eat enough fat
questions.explanation: The complete picture: balanced diet (all nutrients), food safety (preservation), digestion (conversion) — all essential for health.
